selection.scope: Six previously anonymized official-client context-window observations from one listener process.
selection.receipt_join: Each sample time falls within its uniquely matched effect-fenced receipt interval, allowing two seconds on each side; all six distinct trace-and-turn pairs belong to one Keeper.
selection.reaction_join: Each selected receipt interval, extended by three seconds at each end, contains exactly one raw schedule turn-start row for the same source identity.
selection.ledger_window: Rows recorded since the process-start reference and contained in captured readable file prefixes; file reads and the queue snapshot are not atomic.
selection.ledger_sources: Starts and finishes use keeper_event_queue; ACKs and cancellations use keeper_event_queue_transition.

limits: The six sample joins use timestamps; the provider log does not carry the receipt trace identity.
Repeated raw start and finish rows reuse event IDs; the raw row count is not a count of unique IDs.
The pending snapshot, WAL stat and ledger prefixes were read separately while the service was live.
No ACK or cancellation was observed for this identity only within the captured post-start ledger prefixes; this is not a complete-lifetime proof.
An effect-fenced receipt does not establish whether an external effect happened, nor that an external effect was duplicated.
A seventh or later raw reaction can postdate the six originally selected samples.
Turn-start ledger rows do not carry admitted_revision, so matching source identity does not prove that every row names the same queue incarnation.
